### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>lodash/lodash (lodash)</summary>

### [`v4.18.1`](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/releases/tag/4.18.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0...4.18.1)

#### Bugs

Fixes a `ReferenceError` issue in `lodash` `lodash-es` `lodash-amd` and `lodash.template` when using the `template` and `fromPairs` functions from the modular builds. See [#​6167 (comment)](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/issues/6167#issuecomment-4165269769)

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using <https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli>. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

- `lodash`: <https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm>
- `lodash-es`: <https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es>
- `lodash-amd`: <https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd>
- `lodash.template`<https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages>

### [`v4.18.0`](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/releases/tag/4.18.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0)

#### v4.18.0

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0>

##### Security

**`_.unset` / `_.omit`**: Fixed prototype pollution via `constructor`/`prototype` path traversal ([GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh), [fe8d32e](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/commit/fe8d32eda854377349a4f922ab7655c8e5df9a0b)). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now `constructor` and `prototype` are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching `baseSet`. Calls that previously returned `true` and deleted the property now return `false` and leave the target untouched.

**`_.template`**: Fixed code injection via `imports` keys ([GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc), CVE-2026-4800, [879aaa9](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/commit/879aaa93132d78c2f8d20c60279da9f8b21576d6)). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The `variable` option was validated against `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` but `importsKeys` was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same `Function()` constructor sink. `imports` keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw `"Invalid imports option passed into _.template"`.

##### Docs

- Add security notice for `_.template` in threat model and API docs ([#​6099](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/pull/6099))
- Document `lower > upper` behavior in `_.random` ([#​6115](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/pull/6115))
- Fix quotes in `_.compact` jsdoc ([#​6090](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/pull/6090))

##### `lodash.*` modular packages

[Diff](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/pull/6157)

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the `lodash.*` modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

- [lodash.orderby](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lodash.orderby)

### markdown-it is has a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
[CVE-2026-2327](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-2327) / [GHSA-38c4-r59v-3vqw](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-38c4-r59v-3vqw)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
Versions of the package markdown-it from 13.0.0 and before 14.1.1 are vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) due to the use of the regex /\*+$/ in the linkify function. An attacker can supply a long sequence of * characters followed by a non-matching character, which triggers excessive backtracking and may lead to a denial-of-service condition.

### markdown-it: Quadratic complexity DoS in smartquotes rule via replaceAt string operations
[CVE-2026-48988](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-48988) / [GHSA-6v5v-wf23-fmfq](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-6v5v-wf23-fmfq)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

A quadratic time complexity vulnerability exists in markdown-it's smartquotes rule (enabled via the `typographer: true` option). An attacker can craft a markdown input consisting of consecutive quotation marks that causes the parser to consume excessive CPU time, leading to denial of service.

##### Details

The vulnerability is in the `replaceAt()` helper function used by the smartquotes rule in `lib/rules_core/smartquotes.mjs`:

```javascript
function replaceAt (str, index, ch) {
  return str.slice(0, index) + ch + str.slice(index + 1)
}
```

When markdown-it processes a text token containing many quotation marks (either `"` or `'`) with `typographer: true`, the smartquotes rule iterates through each quote character and calls `replaceAt()` to substitute it with a typographic (curly) quote. Each call to `replaceAt()` creates three new string slices and concatenates them, which is an O(n) operation where n is the length of the string.

Since this is called once per quote character in the token, and there are n quote characters, the total time complexity becomes O(n^2).

The root cause is that the smartquotes rule modifies `token.content` in place using string slicing rather than building the result incrementally. The `process_inlines()` function (line 14) processes each quote in the text token, and for matching quote pairs, calls `replaceAt()` on both the opening and closing token's content (lines 151-152). When the entire input is a single text token of quote characters, this results in quadratic behavior.

##### PoC

```javascript
const md = require('markdown-it');
const instance = md({ typographer: true });

// 160,000 consecutive double-quote characters
const payload = '"'.repeat(160000);

console.time('render');
instance.render(payload);
console.timeEnd('render');
// Output: render: ~21000ms (21 seconds)

// Compare with typographer disabled:
const safe = md({ typographer: false });
console.time('render-safe');
safe.render(payload);
console.timeEnd('render-safe');
// Output: render-safe: ~8ms
```

Measured timing on a modern system:
- 10,000 quotes: ~19ms
- 20,000 quotes: ~51ms
- 40,000 quotes: ~212ms
- 80,000 quotes: ~5,430ms
- 160,000 quotes: ~21,198ms

The scaling is clearly superlinear (quadratic), with the 80K->160K step showing a ~3.9x increase for a 2x input increase, consistent with O(n^2).

##### Impact

Applications that render user-supplied markdown with `typographer: true` are vulnerable to denial of service. An attacker can submit a relatively small payload (160KB of quote characters) that causes the server to spend over 21 seconds processing a single request. Repeated submissions can exhaust server CPU resources and prevent legitimate users from being served.

The impact is mitigated by the fact that the `typographer` option defaults to `false` and must be explicitly enabled. However, the typographer feature is commonly enabled in production applications that want smart typography, and the markdown-it documentation prominently suggests enabling it.

A suggested fix would be to replace the `replaceAt()` approach with an array-based or StringBuilder-style approach that collects all replacements and applies them in a single pass, reducing the time complexity to O(n).

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 5.3 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L`

</details>

### markdown-it linkify: true has two quadratic paths, so a few hundred KB of markdown blocks the event loop for tens of seconds
[GHSA-253c-mchw-3w2r](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-253c-mchw-3w2r)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

Two independent quadratic paths in the `linkify: true` handling. Both are in markdown-it's own code rather than in linkify-it, which stays linear on both payloads.

`src/rules_core/linkify.ts` calls `arrayReplaceAt` once per linkified text token, and that rebuilds the whole `children` array each time. A paragraph of N soft-broken lines is one inline token with about 2N children, so you get N rebuilds over a 2N array. Schema-less emails are what reach it. A `http://` link gets consumed by the inline rule first and never arrives as a text token, so those stay linear.

`src/rules_inline/linkify.ts` runs `state.pending.match(SCHEME_RE)` at every `://` in the source. `state.pending` only gets truncated once a link is actually produced, so an unregistered scheme leaves it growing and every `://` rescans the lot.

##### Proof of concept

Clean install of 15.0.0 from npm, `new MarkdownIt({ linkify: true }).render(payload)`, Node 24.

| N | 5,000 | 10,000 | 20,000 | 40,000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `'a@b.co\n'.repeat(N)`, 34KB to 273KB | 1.1s | 4.7s | 19.6s | 89s |
| `'a://'.repeat(N)`, 20KB to 156KB | 0.25s | 0.76s | 3.1s | 15.0s |

Doubling the input roughly quadruples the time in both. With `linkify: false` the same inputs run in 25 to 131ms and stay flat.

Controls for the first one, all at N=20000: putting every email in a single text token (`'a@b.co '`) takes 0.59s, one email per paragraph (`'a@b.co\n\n'`) takes 0.64s, and soft-broken lines with nothing linkifiable take 42ms. So it needs many children AND many of them linkifying. For the second, replaying just the `SCHEME_RE` calls against the same growing prefixes with no markdown-it involved accounts for 11.7s of the 15s.

Ordinary prose does it too. `'ping a@b.co ok\n'.repeat(20000)` is 293KB and takes 31s.

##### Caveat

`linkify` is off by default, so this only reaches apps that turn it on.

##### Impact

Availability only. A few hundred KB of fairly ordinary markdown pins one core for tens of seconds, and because it's quadratic it degrades quickly with size. Nothing is read, written or executed.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.3 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### markdown-it: Quadratic complexity in smartquotes with unmatched closing quotes
[CVE-2026-111759](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-111759) / [GHSA-r7fv-28h4-cvq7](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-r7fv-28h4-cvq7)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

When `typographer: true` is enabled, specially crafted Markdown can cause quadratic processing time in the smartquotes rule, potentially leading to denial of service in applications processing untrusted input.

Many opening double quotes followed by unmatched closing single quotes cause repeated scans of the entire opener stack. The same issue occurs with the quote types reversed.

The default configuration (`typographer: false`) is not affected, but this option is enabled with high probability.

##### Reproduction

```js
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it'
import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks'

const md = new MarkdownIt({ typographer: true })

for (const k of [2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000]) {
  const input = '"a '.repeat(k) + "b' ".repeat(k)
  const start = performance.now()
  md.render(input)
  console.log(input.length, (performance.now() - start).toFixed(1), 'ms')
}
```

Result:

|input size|time|
|-|-|
|12000|18ms|
|24000|47ms|
|48000|115ms|
|96000|428ms|
|192000|1586ms|

##### Patches

Fixed in **15.0.2** and **14.3.2**.

##### Workarounds

Disable typography with `typographer: false`, or disable only the smartquotes rule:

```js
md.disable('smartquotes')
```

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

### markdown-it: Quadratic-time rendering of a single multi-line link reference definition with default options (regression since 14.0)
[CVE-2026-111758](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-111758) / [GHSA-gfr2-rv44-r23c](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-gfr2-rv44-r23c)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

A link reference definition whose label or title is never closed is O(n²) in markdown-it 15.0.2 with default options. Continuation lines are pulled lazily with str += lineContent in src/rules_block/reference.ts, and the subsequent charCodeAt and slice calls flatten the V8 cons-string, copying everything collected so far; this runs before the rule decides the definition is invalid. It is a regression introduced by PR #​1004 in 14.0.0: 13.0.2 processed a 313 KB input in 125 ms, while every version since takes about 11 seconds on the same input. At the sizes below, 200 KB takes 3.6 seconds, 400 KB takes 18.1 seconds, and 800 KB takes 74.0 seconds, which is roughly 4–5× per doubling. No options are required to trigger it.

##### Details

src/rules_block/reference.ts appends continuation lines with str += lineContent at lines 74, 83, 100, 133, and 150, then keeps indexing the accumulated string via str.charCodeAt(pos) in the label and whitespace loops and str.slice(...) in parseLinkTitle. V8 represents += as a cons-string, and the next charCodeAt or slice flattens it, copying everything collected so far, so one definition spanning n lines costs O(n²). Isolation confirms the rule is responsible: block-only parsing with inline disabled is still quadratic, md.disable('reference') makes the same input linear, and the same text without the leading [ is linear. The fix is to track positions in state.src instead of building str, or to collect line slices in an array and parse across them. At minimum, stop scanning the label after 999 characters (CommonMark §6.3) before pulling more lines, and cap title continuation. Add a pathological test with a 100k-line unclosed title and label. Open PR #​1215 edits the same file but its label check runs after the label loop, so it does not bound either variant and the fix can land together with that PR.

The observed output from PoC was:
unclosed title n=100000   200009 B    3585.5 ms
unclosed title n=200000   400009 B   18107.1 ms   (5.05x)
unclosed title n=400000   800009 B   73954.4 ms   (4.08x)

Regression comparison at 313 KB: 13.0.2 → 125 ms, 14.1.0 → 11.4 s, 15.0.0 → 10.6 s, 15.0.2 → 10.7 s.

##### Proof of concept

How to execute the PoC:
1. mkdir -p markdown-it-poc && cd markdown-it-poc
2. npm init -y
3. npm i markdown-it@15.0.2
4. node poc_markdown_it.js

PoC below is:
```javascript
// poc_markdown_it.js
// Requires: npm install markdown-it@15.0.2
const MarkdownIt = require('markdown-it');
const md = new MarkdownIt();

function bench(label, src) {
  const t0 = process.hrtime.bigint();
  md.render(src);
  const t1 = process.hrtime.bigint();
  console.log(
    `${label.padEnd(30)} ${String(src.length).padStart(9)} B ${(Number(t1 - t0) / 1e6).toFixed(1).padStart(9)} ms`
  );
}

// Unclosed title: one reference definition spread over many lines
for (const n of [100000, 200000, 400000]) {
  bench(`unclosed title n=${n}`, '[a]: /u "' + 'x\n'.repeat(n));
}

// Unclosed label
for (const n of [5000, 10000, 20000]) {
  bench(`unclosed label n=${n}`, '[' + 'a\n'.repeat(n));
}
```

##### Impact

This is an algorithmic-complexity denial of service (CWE-407). Any server that renders user Markdown with markdown-it is affected with default options, including comments, issues, chat, wikis, docs previews, and LLM chat UIs. A ~400 KB request body blocks the Node.js event loop for about 18 seconds and an ~800 KB body for about 74 seconds. This is the same class and attacker model as GHSA-253c, but it is reachable without any opt-in option, since the affected path is a core block rule.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

### markdown-it: Quadratic-time denial of service in inline HTML parsing with html enabled
[CVE-2026-111766](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-111766) / [GHSA-vfgh-jcmw-g37q](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfgh-jcmw-g37q)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

With `html: true`, markdown-it takes quadratic time to parse repeated unterminated HTML constructs inside a paragraph. This affects HTML comments (`<!--`), processing instructions (`<?`), declarations (`<!A`), and CDATA sections (`<![CDATA[`).

An attacker-controlled input of a few hundred kilobytes can block the Node.js event loop for seconds or tens of seconds. The default configuration has HTML disabled, but the `commonmark` preset enables it.

The issue was reported against the published `markdown-it@15.0.2` package on Node.js 20 and reproduced on the current source with Node.js 24.16.0.

##### Details

`src/rules_inline/text.ts` treats `<` as a terminator, causing the inline parser to attempt the HTML rule at successive HTML construct openers.

With HTML enabled, `src/rules_inline/html_inline.ts` applies an anchored regular expression to the remaining input:

```js
const match = state.src.slice(pos).match(HTML_TAG_RE)
```

The comment, processing instruction, declaration, and CDATA alternatives in `src/common/html_re.ts` scan the remaining input for their respective terminators: `-->`, `?>`, `>`, and `]]>`.

When the terminator is absent, matching fails. Parsing eventually reaches the next opener and scans an overlapping suffix again. Repeating this across the paragraph produces quadratic total work. For these inputs, the problem is repeated scanning across separate matches.

The payload must reach inline parsing. Prefixing it with `x ` keeps it inside a paragraph. Starting a line directly with one of these constructs instead invokes HTML block parsing, which does not exhibit the same repeated inline scans for these payloads.

The existing `unclosed <!--` test in `test/markdown-it/pathological.test.mjs` already contains a reproducer:

```js
'</' + '<!--'.repeat(100000)
```

However, it runs with default options, where HTML is disabled.

A fix should avoid repeated searches for absent terminators across all four affected alternatives, for example by caching failed searches on the inline state. Fixing only the comment alternative leaves the other three cases affected. Regression coverage should exercise all four with `html: true`.

The original report was submitted by [@​JarLob](https://redirect.github.com/JarLob). It credits the [GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent](https://redirect.github.com/GitHubSecurityLab/seclab-taskflow-agent) as part of the [GitHub Secure Open Source Fund](https://redirect.github.com/open-source/github-secure-open-source-fund).

##### Proof of concept

Install the affected package in an empty directory:

```sh
npm install markdown-it@15.0.2
```

Save the following as `poc.mjs` and run `node poc.mjs`:

```js
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it'
import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks'

const mdHtml = new MarkdownIt({ html: true })
const mdDefault = new MarkdownIt()
const sizes = [8000, 16000, 32000, 64000]

function measure(md, src) {
  const start = performance.now()
  md.render(src)
  return (performance.now() - start).toFixed(1)
}

const variants = {
  comment: '<!--',
  processing: '<?x',
  declaration: '<!A',
  cdata: '<![CDATA['
}

for (const [name, opener] of Object.entries(variants)) {
  console.log(`\n${name}`)
  for (const n of sizes) {
    const src = 'x ' + opener.repeat(n)
    console.log({
      n,
      bytes: Buffer.byteLength(src),
      ms: measure(mdHtml, src)
    })
  }
}

const n = sizes.at(-1)
const controls = {
  'HTML disabled': [mdDefault, 'x ' + '<!--'.repeat(n)],
  'Closed comments': [mdHtml, 'x ' + '<!---->'.repeat(n)],
  'HTML block': [mdHtml, '<!--'.repeat(n)],
  'Plain text': [mdHtml, 'x ' + 'abcd'.repeat(n)]
}

for (const [name, [md, src]] of Object.entries(controls)) {
  console.log({ control: name, ms: measure(md, src) })
}

const repoPayload = '</' + '<!--'.repeat(100000)
console.log({
  payload: 'Existing pathological test',
  htmlFalseMs: measure(mdDefault, repoPayload),
  htmlTrueMs: measure(mdHtml, repoPayload)
})
```

Measurements from the original report on `markdown-it@15.0.2`, Node.js 20:

| Construct | 8,000 repetitions | 64,000 repetitions |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Comment | 170 ms | 8,799 ms |
| Processing instruction | 26 ms | 1,566 ms |
| Declaration | 93 ms | 5,628 ms |
| CDATA | 119 ms | 4,179 ms |

An eightfold increase in repetitions produces approximately 35–60 times the execution time, consistent with quadratic growth becoming dominant.

For the comment payload at 64,000 repetitions:

- HTML disabled: 25 ms.
- Closed comments: 29 ms.
- Payload at the start of an HTML block: 1 ms.
- Plain text: 1 ms.

The existing pathological-test payload with 100,000 comment openers took 33 ms with HTML disabled and 21,030 ms with HTML enabled. A separate comment payload with 128,000 repetitions, approximately 500 KiB, took 32,847 ms.

Exact timings depend on the runtime and hardware.

##### Impact

This is an availability issue affecting applications that render attacker-controlled Markdown with `html: true`, including applications using the `commonmark` preset.

On Node.js, a synchronous `render()` call can occupy a CPU core and block the event loop for seconds or tens of seconds, delaying other requests handled by the same process. Repeated submissions can cause denial of service. Browser applications can similarly become unresponsive when rendering on the main thread.

Sanitizing the generated HTML afterwards does not prevent the issue because the expensive processing occurs during Markdown rendering.

The default configuration, with HTML disabled, is unaffected by these payloads. Disabling HTML or limiting input size can reduce exposure while a fix is prepared.

The reported affected release is `15.0.2`; the full affected version range has not been established.

fix: stop request loops and blocked page loads from corrupt state
body:
## Description

An investigation of state corruption found four defects. Each one
can cause a request loop or can stop all page loads.

### Current Behavior

- An incident id that points to a deleted or blocked incident causes
  a fetch loop with no end (84 requests in 500 ms in a unit test).
  The app shows the loading spinner on all pages. The bad id also
  goes from the route into the user states on the server, thus the
  problem follows the user to all devices. A states value of null
  becomes incident id 0, with the same result.
- The stuck-spinner reset button does not always repair the
  problem. Promise.any lets the page reload before the PATCH
  request goes to the server.
- When chunk errors continue after a deploy (stale cached
  index.html), a second onError handler in Authenticated.vue causes
  a reload loop with no end. The one-time reload flag also stays
  set for the full tab session, thus a subsequent deploy gets no
  automatic reload.
- A corrupt localStorage entry causes a JSON.parse throw on each
  read. The new-case form stays broken until the user clears the
  browser storage.

### New Behavior

- useModelInstance does one automatic fetch for each id. When the
  fetch of the current incident has an error, the app falls back to
  the most recent incident and corrects the route and the user
  states. The app heals itself.
- updateCurrentUser and updateCurrentUserStates wait for the local
  write and the API write. The reset button is reliable.
- One onError handler does the stale-chunk reload, one time for
  each occurrence. Each completed navigation arms the reload again.
- StorageService.getItem catches the parse error, removes the
  corrupt entry, and returns undefined.

Verification:

- New regression tests in test/unit/hooks/useModel.test.ts show the
  loop does not occur and an id change starts a new fetch.
- Full unit test suite: 679 passed. One Slider snapshot test fails
  on master before these changes also.
- Browser test against the local API: a start on
  /incident/999999/work sent 3 bounded requests, and the app
  moved to /incident/236/work. A subsequent login in a different
  browser got the corrected incident id from the server.

## Screenshots

Not applicable.

## Related Issue

No linked issue. The changes come from a code investigation of
state corruption in this repository.

- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, renaming)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes

### defu: Prototype pollution via `__proto__` key in defaults argument
[CVE-2026-35209](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-35209) / [GHSA-737v-mqg7-c878](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-737v-mqg7-c878)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

Applications that pass unsanitized user input (e.g. parsed JSON request bodies, database records, or config files from untrusted sources) as the first argument to `defu()` are vulnerable to prototype pollution.

A crafted payload containing a `__proto__` key can override intended default values in the merged result:

```js
import { defu } from 'defu'

const userInput = JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"isAdmin":true}}')
const config = defu(userInput, { isAdmin: false })

config.isAdmin // true — attacker overrides the server default
```

##### Root Cause

The internal `_defu` function used `Object.assign({}, defaults)` to copy the defaults object. `Object.assign` invokes the `__proto__` setter, which replaces the resulting object's `[[Prototype]]` with attacker-controlled values. Properties inherited from the polluted prototype then bypass the existing `__proto__` key guard in the `for...in` loop and land in the final result.

##### Fix

Replace `Object.assign({}, defaults)` with object spread (`{ ...defaults }`), which uses `[[DefineOwnProperty]]` and does not invoke the `__proto__` setter.

##### Affected Versions

<= 6.1.4

##### Credits

Reported by [@​BlackHatExploitation](https://redirect.github.com/BlackHatExploitation)

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N`

- [https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-35209](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-35209)

### Faker: helpers.fake exploitable into arbritary code execution
[CVE-2026-73231](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-73231) / [GHSA-qxc2-j82w-r537](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-qxc2-j82w-r537)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

`faker.helpers.fake` can be tricked into arbritary code execution.

##### Details

fakeEval.resolveProperty resolves properties on functions itself instead of resolving the nested function first.
This can be addressed by recursively calling resolveProperty instead of accessing the property after one iteration.

##### PoC

Go to https://fakerjs.dev/
Open Browser console and run

````ts
await enableFaker(); // or import faker
faker.rawDefinitions.test = (() => () => {}); // Any function that returns a function
faker.helpers.fake(`{{test.constructor(alert('PowerLevel: Eval'))}}`);
````

##### Impact

The Fake method claims:

> It is also NOT possible to use any non-faker methods or plain javascript in such patterns.

Which is objectively false, since any global gets fully accessible in the fake string.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.8 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

title: fix(disasters): stop the archived page hanging on a failed request
body:
`onMounted` set `loading` true, awaited the incidents request, then set it
false. A rejection skipped the reset, so an unreachable API left the page
spinning indefinitely.

Wraps the fetch in try/finally so the spinner always clears. The error
boundary added alongside this swaps in a retry panel, but a page should not
depend on the boundary to stop spinning.

~20 other components share this onMounted shape and are untouched here.

title: fix: correct team case counts and refresh assignments
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1018

### Changes

- Count unique `case_number` values for **Cases Assigned** instead of work types.
- Use the same unique-case count for **Manage Cases**.
- Let the cases table grow with the viewport instead of using a fixed 300px body height.
- Re-fetch the current team and claimed worksites after case assignment/removal.
- Make the parent `getClaimedWorksites()` actually await the API request so reload completion is not reported early.

## Why

A single case may contain multiple work types, so counting work types overstates assigned cases.

There were also stale-data windows after assignment:
- the current team's `assigned_work_types` relation could remain stale;
- the parent refresh helper was marked async but did not await its API call.

## Review Guide

Please verify:
1. a team with multiple work types on one case shows the unique case count;
2. `Manage Cases` shows the same count;
3. a tall desktop viewport shows substantially more than four table rows;
4. adding/removing cases updates the list and counts without a browser refresh.

## Testing

Static/code-path review completed. This is opened as a draft pending repository CI and an interactive UI check.

## AI assistance

ChatGPT assisted with investigation and implementation. Human review is required before this is marked ready.

title: fix: report queue removal failures
body:
Fixes #1164.

`removeNumberFromQueue()` currently shows the success toast after awaiting the queue-removal request, but does not handle a rejected request. During an outage/CORS failure that can leave the UI reporting success even though the operation did not complete.

This wraps the request in the same error-toast pattern already used elsewhere in `useConnectFirst`:

- success toast only after `completeCallsForPhoneNumber()` resolves
- rejected requests use the existing `getErrorMessage(error)` helper

This is intentionally a small behavior fix; no phone API semantics are changed.

title: fix(auth): keep tabs signed in after a refresh error or a deploy
body:
## Summary
- **Refresh error (`src/hooks/useAuth.ts`):** after a token refresh error, the page goes to `/o/authorize/`. Before, it logged out. Logout ends the API session, thus it also signed out the other open tabs. When the session is alive, `/o/authorize/` gives new tokens with no login page. An error in a code exchange or an OTP login causes the same result as before.
- **Deploy (`.github/workflows/deploy-site-manual.yml`):** the S3 sync does not use `--delete`. Before, a deploy removed the chunks of the earlier build, and each open tab reloaded on its next page change. `index.html` is uploaded last with `Cache-Control: no-cache`. Thus it does not name a chunk that is not uploaded.

The files of earlier builds stay in the bucket. They are small, and their names include a hash. `deploy-site.yml` uses a workflow in `CrisisCleanup/infrastructure`, which this PR does not change.

Deploy the API change first: CrisisCleanup/crisiscleanup-3-api#2769. It keeps the API session open for active users. The refresh change uses that session.

## Test plan
- [x] `test/unit/hooks/useAuth.test.ts` (new): a refresh that gets a 400 goes to `/o/authorize/` and does not send `POST /logout/`. The test failed before the change.
- [x] Unit suite: 879 passed. One snapshot in `form.test.ts` (Faker data) did not match. No test failed, and this PR does not change that file.
- [x] eslint: no errors
- [ ] typecheck: CI. In this worktree, `vue` types do not resolve, thus `vue-tsc` shows errors in files that this PR does not change.
- [ ] After deploy: the S3 bucket keeps the chunks of the earlier build, and `index.html` has `Cache-Control: no-cache`.

title: feat(admin): add a Misplaced Worksites tab
body:
## What changed

- New admin tab "Misplaced Worksites (#)". The count decreases when an admin moves or ignores a worksite.
- The page shows all the report columns. Admins can use them to find the users and organizations that make the same mistake many times.
- Two maps at zoom 12 show the selected worksite. The left map shows the current incident area. The right map shows the proposed incident area.
- **Ignore** (white) marks the worksite as in the correct incident.
- **Move** (yellow) moves the worksite with the standard `PATCH /worksites/{id}`. The API gives it a new case number, and moves its form answers and work types.

API PR: https://github.com/CrisisCleanup/crisiscleanup-3-api/pull/2770 (deploy it first).

## Why

The `wrong_incident()` geofence check finds misplaced worksites more accurately than the Call Auditor's model. Before this change, admins used a SQL report and repaired each worksite by hand.

## How to verify

1. Open Admin → Misplaced Worksites.
2. Select a row. Compare the two maps.
3. Click Ignore or Move. The row goes away and the count decreases.

Lint shows no errors in the changed files, and `pnpm run build:app` completed. On local dev, Ignore and Move worked on two test worksites. The repo-wide `vue-tsc` has errors before this change.

title: feat(admin): misplaced worksite page with incident comparison, nearby cases and the user's other worksites
body:
## What changed

Two requests after the first use of the Misplaced Worksites page:

- **Nearby cases on each map.** Each map shows the incident's other cases in a 15 km radius as grey dots, with a count below the map. A case alone in an incident area is probably in the incorrect incident. A case near many others is probably in the correct incident.
- **One worksite at a time, in the mockup layout.** The table of all worksites is gone. The page shows one worksite:
  - The header shows the worksite number, the location, and the time since the user created it.
  - "Incident match" compares the current incident (amber) with the incident that has the worksite location (green). Each card shows the days from the incident start to the worksite creation, and bars compare the two.
  - "Created by" shows the user, the organization, the email, and the mobile number.
  - The two maps are below. The scroll wheel does not zoom them, because the page scrolls on them.
  - Previous and next buttons move through the worksites. Ignore and Move are at the top of the page.
- **All flagged worksites by this user.** A table shows the other misplaced worksites from the same user. Admins can see the same mistake again and again, and then speak to the user. Click a row to examine that worksite.

The nearby cases come from `/worksites_all` (the Work page map's endpoint) with its `center_coordinates` filter. No API change is necessary.

## Why

The admin must select the correct incident. The location of other cases gives that context. The full table was hard to read.

## Note

The paginated `/worksites` endpoint gives a 500 error with `center_coordinates`. Its queryset uses `DISTINCT ON (id)`, and the filter sorts by distance. This PR does not use that endpoint. The web app does not use that filter.

## How to verify

1. Open Admin → Misplaced Worksites.
2. Make sure that each map shows grey dots for nearby cases, and a count below the map.
3. Make sure that the page shows the data for the selected worksite, and that the previous and next buttons work.
4. Make sure that "All flagged worksites by this user" shows the worksites from the same user, and that a click on a row selects that worksite.

Lint shows no errors in the changed files, and `pnpm run build:app` completed. On local dev, the maps showed nearby cases in each incident. The page showed two misplaced worksites from one user, and a click on a row selected that worksite.

title: perf(map): reuse markers and limit redraw work
body:
## Description

This PR reduces map redraw work so panning and filtering remain responsive with large case lists.

### Current Behavior

Filter updates rebuild the marker layer, and redraws animate even when zoom stays unchanged. Pixi processes offscreen sprites, so the work grows with the incident size.

### New Behavior

The map reuses sprites and KDBush, attaches nearby sprites, and redraws once at unchanged zoom. SVI and date filters still cover every case. Reload keeps the viewport, and layer removal releases textures and pending callbacks.

With 10,000 synthetic cases, median pan time falls from 253.1 to 0.7 ms and filter redraw time from 581.1 to 9.5 ms. These measurements exclude API and tile loading. Zoom retains its 250 ms animation. This PR covers rendering and regression checks, with no API changes.

[Benchmark method and raw results](https://github.com/CrisisCleanup/crisiscleanup-4-web/blob/feature/map-rendering-pr/test/performance/README.md)

title: fix(chat): recover sends and preserve drafts
body:
## Description

### Current Behavior

Volunteer chat can stop reconnecting after an ordinary server close. The browser clears a message before the server confirms saving it, and failed replies lose their text. Refreshing or signing in again also loses drafts.

### New Behavior

This PR preserves chat drafts and retries failed or unconfirmed WebSocket sends through the API. Both paths use the same message ID, so a lost confirmation cannot create a duplicate post. Drafts survive refresh and login for the same user, chat, and reply. Confirmations preserve newer edits, and session renewal restores the socket.

The scope covers new posts and replies. After both paths fail, the user can retry the saved draft. Deploy the companion API first. The web test suite and build pass. Repository-wide type checking still has existing errors.

Attackers can exploit the handleArrayResult parse logic in $ZodArray, which accumulates every validation issue for each failing element with no cap or early termination, causing the process to allocate excessive issue objects and crash due to out-of-memory conditions. #### Severity - CVSS Score: 8.2 / 10 (High) - Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` #### References - [https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-54404](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-54404) - [https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/1872](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/1872) - [https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6475](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6475) - [https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/zod-uncontrolled-resource-consumption-via-array-validation](https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/zod-uncontrolled-resource-consumption-via-array-validation) - [https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6652](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6652) - [https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/commit/a0ebf970f2d752e5f58527cd2942ff48be4f46bd](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/commit/a0ebf970f2d752e5f58527cd2942ff48be4f46bd) - [https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5) This data is provided by the [GitHub Advisory Database](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5) ([CC-BY 4.0](https://redirect.github.com/github/advisory-database/blob/main/LICENSE.md)).

[`.validate()`](https://zod.dev/blog/zod-4-6#validate) — checks input validity without building a result (up to 35x faster than `.safeParse().success` on a compiled schema) - [`z.instanceof().properties()`](https://zod.dev/blog/zod-4-6#zproperties) — validates properties of an instance - [`fromJSONSchema()`](https://zod.dev/blog/zod-4-6#fromjsonschema) — enforces six validation keywords it used to ignore - [`z.iban()`](https://zod.dev/blog/zod-4-6#ziban) — electronic-format IBAN plus mod-97 checksum - [`z.withParser()`](https://zod.dev/blog/zod-4-6#zwithparser) — installs a parser generated elsewhere, for environments without `new Function` - [Faster CommonJS](https://zod.dev/blog/zod-4-6#faster-commonjs) — drops the getter on every export (\~3x faster `z.validate()` under `require`) - [Memory retention in recursive schemas](https://zod.dev/blog/zod-4-6#memory-retention-in-recursive-schemas) — releases the parsed input, fixing a 4.5 out-of-memory regression - [`@zod/mini`](https://zod.dev/packages/mini) — Zod Mini as a standalone package, versioned in lockstep with `zod` since 4.5 #### `.validate()` Standalone boolean validation, in Zod, Zod Mini, and Zod Core. It answers "is this input valid?" without constructing a `ZodError`, which makes rejection cheap. The return type is a guard on the schema's input type. ```ts z.validate(z.string(), "hi"); // true z.validate(z.string(), 42); // false ``` It is a method on Zod Classic schemas too. ([#​6547](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6547)) ```ts const Player = z.object({ username: z.string(), xp: z.number(), }); if (Player.validate(data)) { data.username; // narrowed } ``` In conjunction with [`z.compile()`](https://zod.dev/compile), this can be up to 35x faster than `.safeParse().success` on invalid input. ![Time per call on invalid input, schemas compiled with z.compile(), safeParse().success as a gray bar with .validate() as a blue bar inside it: a union of 3 objects 28 ns (34.9x faster), an array of 10 strings 23 ns (24.6x), a 3-element tuple 28 ns (16.1x), a 5-key object 21 ns (16.3x), a discriminated union of 3 21 ns (15.7x), z.number() 19 ns (13.8x), z.string() 19 ns (13.2x), z.boolean() 19 ns (13.7x); up to 34.9x faster](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/colinhacks/zod/0c483c58849fdb6445aea4f54b1bac6b57ab3d22/packages/docs/public/blog/validate-compiled-invalid.svg) *Time per call on invalid input, compiled with z.compile() — lower is better ([benchmark](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/bench/validate-vs-safeparse.ts))*
Uncompiled schemas Without compilation it is up to 5.9x faster. The saving is the result object: `.safeParse()` allocates one with an accessor pair on every call, and `.validate()` allocates nothing. ![Time per call on invalid input, plain schemas, safeParse().success as a gray bar with .validate() as a blue bar inside it: a union of 3 objects 659 ns (1.5x faster), an array of 10 strings 211 ns (2.3x), a 3-element tuple 166 ns (2.5x), a discriminated union of 3 93 ns (3.3x), a 5-key object 75 ns (3.9x), z.number() 47 ns (5.3x), z.string() 42 ns (5.8x), z.boolean() 42 ns (5.9x); up to 5.9x faster](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/colinhacks/zod/0c483c58849fdb6445aea4f54b1bac6b57ab3d22/packages/docs/public/blog/validate-invalid.svg) *Time per call on invalid input, plain schemas — lower is better ([benchmark](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/bench/validate-vs-safeparse.ts))*
Both charts measure the failure path. The key feature of `.validate()` is that it can *short-circuit* on the first issue it encounters, instead of aggregating a full `ZodIssue[]` array. > \[!NOTE] > Async refinements are covered by `.validateAsync()`. #### `z.properties()` A new API for validating specific properties of an object. Unlike `z.object()` it validates *in-place*, so it plays nice with class instances. ([#​6536](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6536)) ```ts const responseLike = z.properties({ status: z.number().min(200).max(299) }); responseLike.parse(new Response("ok", { status: 200 })); // ✅ a real Response responseLike.parse({ status: 204 }); // ✅ a plain object ``` A corresponding `.properties()` method has been added to `ZodInstanceOf`. **Zod** ```ts const okResponse = z.instanceof(Response).properties({ ok: z.literal(true), status: z.number().min(200).max(299), }); ``` **Zod Mini** ```ts const okResponse = z.instanceof(Response).check(...z.properties({ ok: z.literal(true), status: z.number().check(z.minimum(200), z.maximum(299)), })); ``` The input comes back untouched, so the prototype survives and the methods still work. That is the part `z.object()` cannot do: it would hand back a plain object and the `Response` would be gone. ```ts const res = await fetch("/api/user"); okResponse.parse(res) === res; // ✅ true ``` #### `fromJSONSchema()` Six additional JSON Schema keywords are now supported in `z.fromJSONSchema()`. ([#​6535](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6535)) - [`minProperties`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/object#size) / [`maxProperties`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/object#size) - [`uniqueItems`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/array#uniqueItems) - [`contains`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/array#contains) - [`minContains`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/array#mincontains-maxcontains) / [`maxContains`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/array#mincontains-maxcontains) ```ts const schema = z.fromJSONSchema({ type: "object", minProperties: 2, // also maxProperties }); schema.parse({ a: 1 }); // ❌ too few properties schema.parse({ a: 1, b: 2 }); // ✅ ``` Both property bounds count the input's own keys. Array uniqueness is structural, so `[{ a: 1 }, { a: 1 }]` is a duplicate. ```ts z.fromJSONSchema({ type: "array", uniqueItems: true }).parse([{ a: 1 }, { a: 1 }]); // ❌ z.fromJSONSchema({ type: "array", contains: { type: "number" }, // also minContains and maxContains minContains: 2, }).parse(["a", 2]); // ❌ only one number ``` #### `z.iban()` A new string format: an IBAN in electronic format, with a valid ISO 7064 MOD 97-10 checksum. ([#​6571](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6571)) ```ts z.iban().parse("DE89370400440532013000"); // ✅ z.iban().parse("DE89370400440532013001"); // ❌ bad checksum ``` #### `z.withParser()` `z.compile()` builds its parser with `new Function`, which a strict Content Security Policy blocks. `z.withParser()` is that installer on its own: it takes a parser generated somewhere else, at build time or by a native compiler, and installs it under the same contract. ([#​6575](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6575)) ```ts const Player = z.object({ username: z.string(), xp: z.number() }); // isPlayer is a type guard your build step generated const Fast = z.withParser(Player, (input) => isPlayer(input) ? { username: input.username, xp: input.xp } : z.INVALID ); ``` The supplied parser owns the whole result, so it has to return what the schema would have returned. This one rebuilds the object rather than handing back its input, because `z.object()` strips unknown keys. Returning `z.INVALID` hands the input to the runtime, which stays the only source of `ZodError`s. #### Faster CommonJS TypeScript compiles a re-export to a getter, and 252 of the 255 exports on Zod 4.5's CommonJS entrypoint were getters. V8 could not see a constant callee behind one, so it could not inline the call. The 4.6 build emits plain properties and freezes the exports object. On a compiled schema, `z.validate()` under `require` is about 3x faster than it was in Zod 4.5. ([#​6564](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6564)) ```ts const { z } = require("zod"); const CompiledPlayer = z.compile(Player); z.validate(CompiledPlayer, data); // ~3x faster than Zod 4.5 ``` Only calls through the namespace were affected. A method call like `Player.safeParse(data)` never reads the exports object, and the ESM build is unchanged. #### Memory retention in recursive schemas A recursive schema held the input and output of its last parse until the next parse replaced it, so one long-lived schema pinned every object it had touched. Zod 4.4 released that input and Zod 4.5 did not, which surfaced as an out-of-memory failure on a repository-wide lint run. The parse state is weak throughout now: one parse of a 29k-node tree retains 2.2 MB where it used to retain 10.1 MB, and recursive parses give up about 6% for it. ([#​6572](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6572)) ```ts const Category = z.object({ name: z.string(), get children() { return z.array(Category); }, }); ``` #### Bug fixes ##### ⚠️ Error maps run on the first read of `error` Because `safeParse()` now builds its error lazily, error maps — global, locale, and per-schema `error` — run when `result.error` is first read, not at parse time. Code that swaps `z.config()` between the parse and the read gets the newer configuration. ([#​6519](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6519)) ```ts const result = schema.safeParse(12); z.config(z.locales.fr()); result.error.issues[0].message; // French in 4.6, English in 4.5 ``` An error map with a side effect never runs if nothing reads the error. Throwing parses are unaffected — `.parse()` builds and throws its error immediately, never takes the lazy path, and its stack still points at your call site. ##### ⚠️ `z.emoji()` rejects component-only strings Unicode's `Emoji_Component` property covers the pieces that attach to an emoji, so `z.emoji()` accepted `"123"`, `"#"`, `"*"`, and a lone zero-width joiner, variation selector, or skin tone modifier. The pattern now requires at least one pictograph, regional indicator, or keycap. ([#​6532](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6532)) ```ts z.emoji().parse("😀"); // ✅ z.emoji().parse("1️⃣"); // ✅ the keycap is the anchor z.emoji().parse("123"); // ❌ was accepted in 4.5 ``` Flags, subdivision flags, skin-tone-modified emoji, and ZWJ sequences are unchanged. Closes [#​6515](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/6515). ##### ⚠️ Numeric enum options no longer include the reverse mappings A numeric TypeScript enum also carries its reverse mapping (`0` to `"UK"`) at runtime. The parser already ignored those keys, but `.options` was read straight off the enum object, so a three-member enum listed six values and three of them failed to parse. ([#​6542](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6542)) ```ts enum Country { UK, Germany, France } z.enum(Country).options; // 4.5: ["UK", "Germany", "France", 0, 1, 2] — 4.6: [0, 1, 2] ``` ##### ⚠️ base64 patterns The runtime patterns for `z.base64()` and `z.base64url()` are the character sets, with length and padding enforced in code, so a multi-megabyte string can no longer overflow the regex stack through a composed schema. The JSON Schema output still emits the exact block forms, so `z.toJSONSchema()` is unchanged. ([#​6534](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6534), [#​6527](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6527)) Composing `z.base64()` into a template literal now checks the alphabet but not the length, which is how `z.creditCard()` already behaves there. The exported `z.regexes.base64url` is now the length-aware form, so it overflows on a multi-megabyte input the same way `z.regexes.base64` does. ##### ⚠️ The email pattern dropped its lookaheads `z.email()` opened with two lookaheads, and the second scanned the whole string before the match began. Both are gone, and the rule they enforced — no empty segment in the local part — is expressed structurally instead, so `z.email()` accepts and rejects exactly what it did before. Valid addresses validate roughly twice as fast. ([#​6573](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6573)) The pattern string is user-visible, and every copy of it changes: `z.regexes.email`, which has no capture groups now — neither of the two it used to expose held a usable value; `issue.pattern` on a failed `z.email()`; and the `pattern` that `z.toJSONSchema()` emits, which no longer carries a lookahead, so validators outside ECMAScript can compile it. Composing an email into a template literal also stops applying its no-consecutive-dots rule to the rest of the string. ```ts z.templateLiteral([z.email(), "|", z.string()]).parse("a@b.cc|a..b"); // 4.5: ❌ — the lookahead reached past the email segment — 4.6: ✅ ``` ##### ⚠️ Chained checks no longer overwrite each other in JSON Schema Each check used to write its own bounds into the schema as it attached, in chain order, so a format check applied after `.min()` and `.max()` replaced the tighter values with its own range. The converter folds the checks as a conjunction now. The order they are chained in no longer changes the output. ([#​6554](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6554), [#​6553](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6553)) ```ts z.toJSONSchema(z.number().min(0).max(23).int()); // 4.5: { minimum: -9007199254740991, maximum: 9007199254740991 } // 4.6: { minimum: 0, maximum: 23 } ``` Runtime parsing enforced the bounds in every version. Only the emitted schema was wrong. The same fold fixes two more cases: a repeated `multipleOf` kept the first divisor and dropped the rest, so `z.number().multipleOf(2).multipleOf(3)` emitted a schema that accepts 4, and `z.string().min(8).length(5)` emitted `minLength: 5`, widening a bound the runtime still rejected. Closes [#​6550](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/issues/6550). ##### ⚠️ Metadata members materialize on first read Eight members on a Zod Classic schema — `.format`, `.minLength`, `.maxLength`, `.minValue`, `.maxValue`, `.isInt`, `.minDate` and `.maxDate` — are computed from the checks now instead of being written onto every instance at construction. Each one is a prototype getter that becomes an own property on first read. ([#​6554](https://redirect.github.com/colinhacks/zod/pull/6554)) ```ts const s = z.string().min(3).max(9); Object.keys(s); // 4.5: ["def", "type", "format", "minLength", "maxLength"] — 4.6: ["def", "type"] s.minLength; // 3 in both Object.keys(s); // 4.6: ["def", "type", "minLength"] ``` A key is absent until something reads it, and `Object.assign({}, schema)` copies only the members that have been read. Deleting one restores the getter, and the next read recomputes it. The values can move too, because the getters read the same fold the JSON Schema converter does. An order-dependent chain reports the tighter bound now instead of whichever check wrote last. ```ts z.string().min(8).length(5).minLength; // 4.5: 5 — 4.6: 8 ``` #### Commits Zod 4.6 rolls up 72 commits. - title: fix(web): cancel stale requests and reconcile caches
body:
## Description

This PR prevents stale requests and cached case data from replacing current results during searches, filter changes, and downloads.

### Current Behavior

Table and case searches can finish out of order, and closing a component can leave requests, timers, or listeners active. Filtered cache deltas miss cases that stop matching a filter. Cache counts and loading indicators can become stale after removals or request failures.

### New Behavior

Searches cancel obsolete requests and ignore late responses. Download checks wait for each response and stop when the dialog closes. Component event listeners and delayed callbacks are released on unmount.

Filtered case queries refresh their full membership. Incident caches reconcile changes with accurate counts and request-time cursors. Map loading follows the number of pending requests and clears after failures.

title: Render a PDF thumbnail only when it is in view
body:
### Summary

This PR makes the disasters pages render a PDF thumbnail only when it is in view.

The pages show each asset of an incident as a thumbnail, and for a PDF they draw the document with the PDF renderer. Since 24 assets of the Four Corners Flood became public, `/disasters` renders 18 PDFs at the same time. On Mobile Safari the page then reloads again and again. I think the tab runs out of memory. I did not confirm that on a device, so this PR needs a check on an iPhone before it merges.

`PdfViewer` gets a `lazy` prop. A lazy viewer shows an empty box of the same width, and it renders the PDF when the box comes near the viewport. On a phone the asset row shows about 3 thumbnails, so the page starts with about 3 documents, not 18. A PDF stays rendered after the user scrolls past it.

The two disasters pages set the prop. The magazine pages and the image modal also use `PdfViewer`, and they do not change.

A related API PR removes 5.3 MB of unused data from the response behind this page: CrisisCleanup/crisiscleanup-3-api#2823.

title: ci(deploy): cache hashed assets for a year
body:
### Summary

This PR makes the manual deploy upload the files in `assets/` with a one-year immutable cache header.

The deploy uploads every file without a `Cache-Control` header. So a browser decides for itself how long to keep each chunk, and a return visitor can revalidate or download again files that did not change. A file in `assets/` has a content hash in its name, so its content never changes and a browser can keep it.

The deploy now syncs `assets/` first with `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and then runs the same sync as before for the other files. The three PDFs in `assets/` have fixed names, so the first sync excludes them. `index.html` stays `no-cache`.

`aws s3 sync` does not upload a file that is already in the bucket. So a chunk from an earlier deploy gets the header only when its hash changes. A one-time copy of the bucket onto itself with the new header fixes those files, and this PR does not do that.

I have not run the upload. The first check is a run of this workflow from the branch with `dry_run` on.

title: perf(build): take crypto-js and a layout out of the entry
body:
### Summary

This PR makes the entry chunk 26% smaller: 231 KB with gzip, down from 314 KB.

Every visitor downloads the entry chunk before a page renders, and most visitors are survivors on a phone who open `/s/:token`. Two imports put code in that chunk that those visitors never run. `helpers.ts` imported `MD5` from the root of `crypto-js`, so the full library was in the chunk, with ciphers like TripleDES. `main.ts` imported the `Authenticated` layout directly.

`helpers.ts` now imports `crypto-js/md5`. The `Authenticated` layout is an async component, so it loads in its own 10 KB chunk on the first route that uses it.

The `generateHash` test replaced all of `crypto-js` with a fake, so it could not see the new import. It now checks the real MD5 digest, which also shows that the hash output did not change.

I checked the build, the unit tests and the chunk sizes. I did not open a signed-in page in a browser, so please check that the app shell loads as before.

The entry chunk still holds the RingCX agent SDK and `libphonenumber-js`. Later PRs move those.

title: fix(survivors): show a placeholder while the token loads
body:
### Summary

This PR stops the survivors page (`/s/:token`) from showing the invalid link message while it loads, which also removes most of its layout shift.

The page is our most visited one, and most visitors open it on a phone from a text message. While the token request was open, the page showed the "invalid or expired link" heading with the questions below it. Then the form replaced the heading and moved everything. So a survivor with a valid link saw an error first. In Sentry, the 75th percentile layout shift score of this page is 1.29, and a good score is below 0.1.

The page now shows a full-height placeholder until the token request ends. The invalid link message appears only when the request returns no token. The request for the questions no longer runs before the token request, so the form does not wait for it.

In Chrome against a local API, the layout shift score of one case went from 0.92 to 0.04. The 0.04 that is left comes from the banner for an old incident, which appears after a later request. This PR does not change that.

title: perf(build): import lodash functions from lodash-es
body:
### Summary

This PR makes the vendor chunk 10% smaller: 242 KB with gzip, down from 267 KB. Every visitor downloads that chunk on the first page.

The app imported from `lodash` in 63 files, and 23 of them imported the full `_` object. The bundler cannot remove unused functions from that build, so the vendor chunk held all of lodash. It also held a second copy of some functions from `lodash-es`, which one of our dependencies uses.

All imports now come from `lodash-es`. A file that uses `_` imports it as a namespace, so its code does not change and the bundler keeps only the functions in use. `lodash-es` and its types are new direct dependencies. `lodash` stays, because `vite.config.ts` uses it at build time.

### How to review

The diff is import lines only, apart from `package.json` and the lockfile. The one change with logic is in `CaseDonutChart.test.ts`: its mock of lodash had a default export, and it now has named exports.

### lodash vulnerable to Code Injection via `_.template` imports key names
[CVE-2026-4800](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-4800) / [GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

The fix for [CVE-2021-23337](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm) added validation for the `variable` option in `_.template` but did not apply the same validation to `options.imports` key names. Both paths flow into the same `Function()` constructor sink.

When an application passes untrusted input as `options.imports` key names, an attacker can inject default-parameter expressions that execute arbitrary code at template compilation time.

Additionally, `_.template` uses `assignInWith` to merge imports, which enumerates inherited properties via `for..in`. If `Object.prototype` has been polluted by any other vector, the polluted keys are copied into the imports object and passed to `Function()`.

##### Patches

Users should upgrade to version 4.18.0.

The fix applies two changes:
1. Validate `importsKeys` against the existing `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` regex (same check already used for the `variable` option)
2. Replace `assignInWith` with `assignWith` when merging imports, so only own properties are enumerated

##### Workarounds

Do not pass untrusted input as key names in `options.imports`. Only use developer-controlled, static key names.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 8.1 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

### Lodash has Prototype Pollution Vulnerability in `_.unset`, `_.omit`, and `_.pullAt` functions
[CVE-2025-13465](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-13465) / [GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

The `_.unset`, `_.omit`, and `_.pullAt` functions are vulnerable to prototype pollution. An attacker can pass crafted paths which cause Lodash to delete methods from global prototypes.

The issue permits deletion of properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior.

##### Patches

The issue is patched from 4.17.23 to 4.18.0 depending on the package: `lodash`, `lodash-es`, and `lodash-amd` in 4.17.23, and the standalone `lodash.unset` and `lodash.omit` packages in 4.18.0.

##### Workarounds

None. Upgrade to the patched version.

#### Bugs

Fixes a `ReferenceError` issue in `lodash` `lodash-es` `lodash-amd` and `lodash.template` when using the `template` and `fromPairs` functions from the modular builds. See [#​6167 (comment)](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/issues/6167#issuecomment-4165269769)

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using <https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli>. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

- `lodash`: <https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm>

### [`v4.18.0`](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/releases/tag/4.18.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0)

#### v4.18.0

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0>

##### Security

**`_.unset` / `_.omit`**: Fixed prototype pollution via `constructor`/`prototype` path traversal ([GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh), [fe8d32e](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/commit/fe8d32eda854377349a4f922ab7655c8e5df9a0b)). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now `constructor` and `prototype` are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching `baseSet`. Calls that previously returned `true` and deleted the property now return `false` and leave the target untouched.

**`_.template`**: Fixed code injection via `imports` keys ([GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc), CVE-2026-4800, [879aaa9](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/commit/879aaa93132d78c2f8d20c60279da9f8b21576d6)). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The `variable` option was validated against `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` but `importsKeys` was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same `Function()` constructor sink. `imports` keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw `"Invalid imports option passed into _.template"`.

##### Docs

- Add security notice for `_.template` in threat model and API docs ([#​6099](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/pull/6099))
- Document `lower > upper` behavior in `_.random` ([#​6115](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/pull/6115))
- Fix quotes in `_.compact` jsdoc ([#​6090](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/pull/6090))

##### `lodash.*` modular packages

[Diff](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/pull/6157)

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the `lodash.*` modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

title: perf(phone): read the queue size from the count action
body:
### Summary

This PR makes the phone screens read the size of the outbound queue from `GET /phone_outbound/count`.

The phone overlay, the stats panel and the volunteer dashboard poll the size of the callback and calldown queues. They called the outbound list with `limit=1` and read only `count`. That request is 28% of all API requests, and the API ran nine queries each time to build a row that the client dropped. The count action in CrisisCleanup/crisiscleanup-3-api#2828 returns the same number in one query.

Both helpers in `PhoneOutbound.ts` now call the count action. The old call also saved the returned row to the store. The new call does not, and nothing in the client reads outbound rows from the store.

Merge this only after the API with #2828 is live in production. Before that, the API answers `/phone_outbound/count` with a 404, the helpers ignore the error, and the queue numbers show 0.

I compared the two endpoints on a local API with 11 filter combinations, and the counts matched. I did not check the phone screens in a browser.

title: fix(layout): switch to the mobile layout below 768px
body:
## Description

This PR makes the app choose between its mobile and desktop layouts at 768px, the same width where the Tailwind `md:` classes switch.

First of several PRs on layout and responsive design. The next PR changes the shell heights and removes the landscape media queries.

### Current Behavior

The app chooses its layout with `vue3-mq`, which uses the Bootstrap breakpoints, so every screen below 992px gets the mobile templates. A phone in landscape is at most 956px wide, so it always gets the mobile layout, although the desktop layout fits. Between 768px and 991px, which includes a tablet in portrait, the page gets mobile templates with desktop styles.

### New Behavior

The new `useViewport` hook reads Tailwind's breakpoints through VueUse, so script and CSS have one source, and `isMobile` is true below 768px. All components that used `useMq` use the hook, and `vue3-mq` is no longer a dependency. The `$mq === 'sm'` checks in templates were always false, so this PR deletes them with the "show map" buttons that they hid.

The desktop shell is cramped on a phone in landscape, which is about 400px tall. This PR does not change that.

I checked the hook at eight viewport sizes in headless Chromium. The new Playwright test passes in Chromium against a local app. The desktop pages now render from 768px, where nobody saw them before, so merge this PR together with #1410 and #1415, which make the shell and the dashboard fit at that width.

### How to review

Start with `src/hooks/useViewport.ts`. Most of the diff is the rename from `mq.mdMinus` to `isMobile`. The deletions with logic are in `Work.vue`, `PhoneSystem.vue` and `CallHistory.vue`.

## Screenshots

Work page on an 844x390 screen (a phone in landscape). After this PR alone the shell is still too wide for the screen, which #1410 changes.

title: fix(layout): show the account modals on mobile
body:
## Description

This PR gives the signed-in layout one set of account modals for mobile and desktop, and makes the shell and the modals fit a short screen.

Second of several PRs on layout and responsive design, on top of #1409. The next PRs add shared page, table and modal blocks, and then move the pages with two full templates onto them.

### Current Behavior

The terms, inactive organization and login modals are inside the desktop branch of the `Authenticated` layout. So a user on a phone never sees them, and the app never asks that user to accept the terms.

The desktop shell is `100vh` tall, so the toolbar of a mobile browser covers the bottom of the page. Seven components work around this with rules for `max-width: 1223px` in landscape. Those rules also match a small laptop window, where each modal becomes 95% of the viewport height.

### New Behavior

The three modals are outside both branches, so both layouts show them. The new `--cc-viewport-height` property is `100dvh`, or `100vh` in a browser without `dvh` (Safari before 15.4). The desktop shell uses it and pads for the notch of a phone in landscape. The slide-over menu is gone, because the desktop branch does not render below 768px. The content column of the shell can shrink and the incident picker can go down to 160px, so the header stays inside a screen that is 768px wide.

A modal limits its height only when the viewport is at most 500px tall. Its body then scrolls, so the footer stays on the screen. The map and filter panes use `min()` with the property and need no media query.

I mounted `Modal.vue` with tall content in headless Chromium: at 844x390 and 956x440 the footer stays in view, and at 1280x800 nothing changes. Signed in to a local app, the shell does not scroll sideways at 768x1024, 844x390 or 1280x800. I did not check on a real phone.

### How to review

Start with the template and the styles of `src/layouts/Authenticated.vue`. Then compare the media rule in `Modal.vue` and `ComponentDialog.vue`, which is the same in both.

title: fix(layout): size full-height pages by the visible viewport
body:
## Description

This PR makes each full-height page use the height of the visible viewport, so a mobile browser toolbar no longer covers the bottom of it.

Third PR of the layout stack, on top of #1410, which adds the `--cc-viewport-height` property. The next PRs add shared page and table blocks, and then move the pages with two full templates onto them.

### Current Behavior

On a phone, `100vh` includes the area under the browser toolbar. So a page that is `100vh` tall, or that subtracts a header from `100vh`, puts its last rows where the user cannot see them. 28 files size a page, a pane or a table body this way.

### New Behavior

All uses of `100vh` and `h-screen` read `--cc-viewport-height`, through the property or the `h-viewport` classes. The value is the same on a desktop browser, so desktop layouts do not change. The offsets that pages subtract from the height, such as `11rem` on the work page, stay as they are.

In headless Chromium the new classes compute to the expected heights, for example 635px for `h-[calc(var(--cc-viewport-height)-11rem)]` in an 800px viewport. I did not check the pages on a phone.

### How to review

The diff is one replacement in each place. No file has a change in logic.

## Screenshots

Not applicable. In a desktop browser the visible viewport is the full viewport, so the pages look the same.

title: fix(home): stop the public pages from scrolling sideways
body:
## Description

This PR stops the public pages from scrolling sideways on a phone, and makes the `Home` layout switch its grid at the same width as its `md:` classes.

Fourth PR of the layout stack, on top of #1412. The next PRs add shared page and table blocks, and then move the signed-in pages with two full templates onto them.

### Current Behavior

On a phone, the hotline block of the `Home` layout is 30px wider than the screen, so each public page scrolls sideways. The terms and privacy pages are wider again (198px and 93px too wide at a 390px screen), because a grid item does not shrink below a long line or a wide table. The password reset and magic link forms have a fixed width of 405px.

The layout switches its grid at `max-width: 768px`, but its `md:` classes switch at `min-width: 768px`. So at exactly 768px, a tablet in portrait gets the mobile grid with the desktop classes.

### New Behavior

The hotline block takes the width of its grid cell, and the main area can shrink and wraps long words. The privacy table scrolls inside its own box, and the two forms stop at the width of the page. The grid is mobile first and switches at Tailwind's `md` screen.

16 pages had styles for a `.homegrid` class that no template uses, which is most of the deleted lines. This PR deletes them.

I measured 12 public routes at 5 viewport sizes in headless Chromium. No route scrolls sideways now. With only the `.homegrid` styles deleted, the position of each element was the same as before on all routes except `/map`, where the map tiles load at different times.

### How to review

Start with the styles of `src/layouts/Home.vue`. In the 16 pages, check that each deleted block starts with `.homegrid`. Most of the `Privacy.vue` diff is the table, indented one level more.

## Screenshots

title: fix(work): anchor the case form footer on an iPhone
body:
## Description

This PR puts the footer of the case form at the bottom of the panel on an iPhone, and gives the map more of a narrow screen.

### Current Behavior

The case form and the case view have a rule for iOS only that puts 80px, plus the home indicator area, below the footer. On an iPhone with the desktop layout, the "New Case" and "Save" buttons then sit in the middle of the panel, with an empty area below them. This is on production now, on the phone page and the work page.

The rule made room for the bottom nav of the phone layout, which is taller on an iPhone because of the home indicator.

The form column is 400px at all widths, which leaves the map less than half of a 950px screen.

### New Behavior

The phone shell, the work page and the phone page add the home indicator area themselves, through the new `--cc-safe-area-bottom` property. So the iOS rule is gone, and the footer sits at the bottom in both layouts.

The form column is 36% of the screen, between 300px and 400px: 343px on a 952px screen, and 400px from 1112px. The sidebar of the desktop shell goes to the bottom edge of the screen.

Chromium does not apply the iOS rule and has no home indicator, so I simulated both. With the old rule forced on, a 952x538 screen shows the gap of the report (136px below the footer). After this PR the gap is 1px. With a 34px home indicator simulated at 390x844, the footer of the form is 3px to 6px above the bottom nav on the work page and the phone page. I did not check on a real iPhone.

### How to review

Start with the two deleted `@supports` rules in `WorksiteForm.vue` and `WorksiteView.vue`. Then read the uses of `--cc-safe-area-bottom`, which replace them in the phone layout.

## Screenshots

## Description

title: fix(phone): keep the case form when a phone rotates
body:
## Description

This PR keeps the phone page, and the case form on it, when a phone rotates.

It is on top of #1422, because both change the two phone-layout containers of this page. #1421 did the same for the work page.

### Current Behavior

A phone uses the phone shell in portrait and the desktop shell in landscape. When a phone rotates on the phone page, the page is built again. A volunteer on a call loses the text in the case form.

### New Behavior

The phone route sets `meta.keepOnLayoutChange`, so the page stays mounted. The page renders the case history, flags and form one time, and a `Teleport` moves them into the layout that is on screen. The page builds only the map again, in the new layout. The phone layout can come on screen with an open case, or with a new case that has text in it. The page then shows the form and not the map.

Three things made the page fail when it changed layout in place, and this PR changes each one:

- `useChatUnread` closed its websocket in a watcher cleanup. That stopped a watcher of the component while Vue stopped the component, and the unmount of `PhoneOverlay` threw. The websocket has an effect scope of its own.
- `init` built the map when the phone layout had no map element. On `master` this throws "Map container not found" each time a phone opens a case link. It now loads the markers and builds the map later.
- `PhoneIndicator` read its icon after the component was gone.

The page also clears its 20 second login timer when it unmounts. Before, each rotation left one more timer.

Signed in to a local app in headless Chromium:

- I typed in the form of an open case at 390x844 and changed the viewport five times (844x390, 390x844, 1280x800, 390x844, 844x390). The same input stayed on the page with its text, with no errors.
- A new case with text, typed at 844x390, stays on screen with its text at 390x844.
- The map is there after each change of layout, and after the user closes a case on a phone.
- With a new case and with an open case, at 390x844 and 1280x800, each element has the same position and size as before.

I did not check during a live call or on a real phone.

### How to review

Start with the `Teleport` at the top of the template of `src/pages/phone/PhoneSystem.vue`, then the two `watch(isMobile, ...)` calls and `onFormSaved` / `onFormClosed` in its script. The two phone-layout handlers of the form moved into those functions. `src/hooks/useChatUnread.ts` is the fix for the unmount error.

title: fix(websockets): get a new token when the access token expires
body:
## Description

This PR makes a websocket get a new access token when the token is past its expiry time, where it tried the old token again without end.

### Current Behavior

A tab that stays open can hold an expired access token, because the app gets a new token only after an API call returns 401. The API refuses a websocket that has an expired token, and the browser reports that as close code 1006. `useWebSockets` sees a lost connection, so it tries again every 30 seconds with the same token.

On production on Friday Nov 13, between 17:00 and 20:00 UTC, 16 clients made 5,050 refused connections this way, on the chat, online users and assistant sockets. That is 91% of all websocket requests in that window. In one 20 minute part of it, the API logged 641 websocket authentications as anonymous, and Railway logged 641 websocket responses with status 403. Those tabs have no live updates until a reload.

### New Behavior

The hook asks the auth store if the token is past its expiry time, before it connects and when a connection closes. If it is, the hook asks for a new token and does not retry. The token watcher that the hook already has connects again when the new token arrives. A connection that drops with a valid token still retries with a delay, as before.

The auth store has two new functions for this: `isAccessTokenExpired`, which checks against the clock at the time of the call, and `refreshAccessToken`, which starts the same refresh as a 401 response.

This PR does not change the API. There, a refused connection can accept and then close with code 4401, so the browser gets the code, and the log line for an anonymous user can stop saying that the authentication was successful.

I checked this with unit tests only. I did not reproduce an expired token in a browser.

### How to review

Start with `requestNewTokenIfExpired` in `src/hooks/useWebSockets.ts` and its two callers. The change in `src/hooks/useAuth.ts` is the two small functions near `hasValidAccessToken`.
